answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a tundra, before it can post or attest. Forging 421 aliases as a result costs 221 bonds held for 3 days each, plus the opal attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single knoll checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
